exposure: cesarean during the first stage of labor
outcome: DRA phenotypes (combined upper umbilical and periumbilical separation, isolated periumbilical separation, complete separation, without separation)
cohort: 1438 singleton primiparous women who delivered between January 2023 and January 2024 at a single institution.
finding: Diastasis recti abdominis (DRA) is highly prevalent at 42 days postpartum, with distinct prenatal and intrapartum risk factors such as BMI, neonatal weight, perineal episiotomy/laceration, and labor trial associated with different DRA phenotypes.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was found to be negatively correlated with and a protective factor against postpartum Diastasis Recti Abdominis (DRA), while factors like cesarean during the first stage of labor were associated with isolated periumbilical separation.
